conclusions: The five splice functional negatives have independent direct counterexamples to the fixed contract.
Complex shifting-derived negatives may still resource-fail; never credit that as an ordinary proof-failure control.
The missing filter invariant leaves executable behavior unchanged.
Helper falsity is independent; passing-client/unproved-helper requires actual named caller success.
Omission controls require exact input/inventory rejection even if native exits zero.
No minimality, causal ablation, necessary-call, model-difficulty or held-out inference.

controls.interpretation: Recursive pop/filter/reappend preserves stable order and exact removed count by induction on old size. Native proof remains required.
Leaves the initial sequence unchanged.
Retains a value equal to the strict threshold.
Compacts but does not remove the discarded tail.
Writes to the read index rather than closing the gap.
Executable operations are identical to the qualified filter reference; only a proof invariant is removed. A failure would be proof-support sensitivity, and a pass must be preserved.
Exact filter-empty source is staged but the addition is excluded from native roots. Coverage must reject even exit zero.
Returns without performing the range edit.
Forward source order with backward destinations reverses the copied tail even on a nonoverlapping example.
Replacement overwrites the preserved prefix rather than starting at position.
The changed final loop never shrinks the array from its working size.
The array never grows in a strict-growth case; the size assertion is false and a later Put is out of range.
AppendAll returns without appending. Its caller remains the resource-heavy shifting body; caller success cannot be presumed.
Exact splice-empty source is staged but the addition is excluded from native roots. Coverage must reject even exit zero.
Count zero must succeed for any input; unconditional failure violates the biconditional.
Only one frame is parsed when two are required.
Exact counted-always-failure source is staged but its addition is omitted.
The payload order is reversed, violating exact re-encoding.
ReadU16Frame always fails despite a valid empty frame; caller outcomes require actual named-unit evidence.
Discards a nonempty trailing suffix after the requested frames.
A matching tag with empty payload/companion and adequate budget must succeed.
Returns the tag as payload rather than removing exactly that byte.
Exact tagged-always-failure source is staged but its addition is omitted.
Returns success when decoded payload length exceeds the supplied budget.
Returns success despite a mismatched first payload byte.
ReadFramePair always fails for two valid empty frames; caller outcomes require actual named-unit evidence.
